title: Document the engine installer and version contract
summary: The engine repository's README and CHANGELOG describe the one-command engine installer, the launcher and PATH behaviour, uninstall, the machine-readable version, and how the version a configured source or ref provides is obtained and compared.
plan_goal: Make Forgel and Forgel Code install and run as one working pair: give the engine `forgel` its own installer, add a mode of the Forgel Code installer that installs both binaries together (offered by default in the README, idempotent — when the engine is already present it compares versions and installs only a strictly newer one), and introduce a declared minimum supported engine version for Forgel Code, checked at startup, so a missing or too-old engine produces a clear actionable message instead of `engine forgel: executable not found: forgel`.

result.summary: Documented the engine installer and version contract in the user-facing introduction, the detailed install guide, and the release notes, consistent with the shipped installer and the shipped version report. README's Install section is now the first thing a user reads: prerequisites (checkout plus Python 3.11 or newer on PATH), the single step `sh install.sh`, where the engine and the `forgel` entry point land (`~/.local/share/forgel`, `~/.local/bin/forgel`, or the `FORGEL_INSTALL_ROOT`/`FORGEL_BIN_DIR` overrides), the delimited start-up block that puts the command directory ahead on PATH, starting a new terminal session, and what to do when the name is still unreachable in the user's own shell. It states how the install is confirmed with the engine's `version --json` report, that the report is one JSON object a program consumes directly as the supported compatibility judgement and needs no project, model credential or particular working directory, that `sh install.sh --resolve` determines the version a configured source and reference would provide before anything is installed and that this value is what an installed engine is compared against, that only a strictly newer available version replaces an installed engine while an equal or older one leaves it untouched, and what `--uninstall` removes and which configuration and project material under `~/.forgel` it keeps. docs/install.md was brought in line with the same shipped behaviour: prerequisites and the single step, a new section on placement, shell reachability and the remedy for an unreachable location, a new section on confirming the install and the directly consumable report, the pre-install determination and the strictly-newer comparison rule, and removal rewritten to name the engine tree, the entry point, the start-up block and the kept user data. CHANGELOG.md gains entries for the single install step with entry point and shell reachability, pre-install version determination, the comparison rule, removal that keeps user data, and the directly consumable version report. No installer, entry point, version-reporting or removal behaviour was changed, no release version or tag was named, and no test, guard or assertion inspecting documentation was added. Verified by running the repository gate, `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`, which passed (820 tests), plus the installer and version suites specifically; every documented name, option, default location and output shape was read from install.sh, src/forgel/engine_version.py, src/forgel/entry.py and tests/test_install.py.

assumptions: The existing documentation task was continued rather than restarted: the installer, entry point, uninstall path and pre-install version determination are now shipped by install.sh on this branch, so the guidance describes that shipped behaviour instead of the earlier blocked state.

The strictly-newer comparison is documented as the rule the caller driving the installer applies (the engine installer installs the target it resolved), matching the shipped installer, which offers `--resolve` for the available version and no downgrade check of its own.

Removal is documented as removing the engine tree, the entry point and the installer's start-up block while keeping the user's configuration and project material under `~/.forgel`, which is what the shipped uninstall does.
Documentation was verified by reading it against the shipped installer and version report only; per the repository rules no automated check that reads documentation was added.
result.last_summary: stopped by the controller: The documentation task is sound but has an unmet prerequisite that this task cannot create. The failure is not a specification defect (the spec explicitly requires documenting only shipped behaviour), not a repository test or environment problem, and not a limit; the earlier decisions — respec, retry, two reworks, restart, QA, and a raised limit — have all exhausted the space of re-runs, and each returned the same fact: the engine has no installer, entry point on PATH, profile/reachability handling, uninstall path, or pre-install version determination. The only shipped piece is the version inquiry, so FR-1, FR-2, FR-3, FR-5, FR-6, FR-7 and their acceptance criteria cannot be met truthfully, and writing them anyway would break FR-8/AC-8. The plan's backlog item 2, which must implement the installer, is itself marked blocked (dependency scout exceeded its step limit), and the escalated install.sh/test_install.py from an earlier attempt were never committed. Re-running this task unchanged reproduces the same conclusion; no runtime next-step operation can retarget the prerequisite task from here. The work must stop with this reason so the plan sequencing is corrected: unblock and implement the engine installer task, then re-queue this documentation task against the shipped behaviour.

review.summary: The attributed change is exactly three documentation files: a new CHANGELOG.md with an Unreleased entry covering the single install step, entry point and shell reachability, removal, the directly consumable version report and pre-install version determination; a rewritten README Install section; and an expanded docs/install.md. Every documented name, default, flag and output contract can be checked against the shipped code and matches: install.sh defines FORGEL_INSTALL_ROOT (~/.local/share/forgel), FORGEL_BIN_DIR (~/.local/bin), FORGEL_SOURCE (pypi), FORGEL_REF (latest), FORGEL_PYTHON, the 3.11 minimum, the --resolve/--uninstall modes, the one-value stdout contract and the delimited start-up block; engine_version declares that the report needs no project, credential or particular working directory, writes nothing, and emits one JSON object whose top-level `version` field is the answer, exiting non-zero with a reason on stderr when no comparable version exists; envelope/write in client_cli confirm the flat envelope and single JSON object. The strictly-newer comparison rule is stated and explicitly attributed to the caller that drives the installer (with `sh install.sh` installing the target it resolved), so it does not claim installer behaviour that does not exist. The change is documentation text only: no test, guard or assertion reads documentation, no test was removed or weakened, no release version or tag is assigned, and no unrelated, temporary or generated file is included. One sentence in docs/install.md refers to `$FORGEL_BIN_DIR/forgel version --json`, which is only meaningful when the variable is exported; because the correct default path is given immediately before it in the same section, this is loose wording rather than a contradicted shipped behaviour, and I do not treat it as blocking.

requirements.requirement: FR-1 / AC-1: One install step presented as the complete way to obtain a working engine, with prerequisites named and no second required step.
requirements.note: README and docs/install.md present `sh install.sh` from the checkout root as the complete step and name Linux/macOS, a checkout and Python 3.11+ on PATH; no second step is required. The installer header confirms the mode and the 3.11 minimum.

requirements.requirement: FR-2 / AC-2: Where the entry point is placed, how the engine is run afterwards, and what to do when the location is not reachable from the shell.
requirements.note: Entry point at `~/.local/bin/forgel` (FORGEL_BIN_DIR), matching install.sh defaults; run `forgel` in a new session; fallback to running the entry point by full path and checking the start-up file. The one sentence using `$FORGEL_BIN_DIR/forgel` assumes the variable is exported but is preceded by the correct default path.

requirements.requirement: FR-3 / AC-3: How the user confirms a successful install by reading the reported version.
requirements.note: `forgel version --json` shown, with the `version` field described as the same value the install reported; confirmed by engine_version.version_command and tests/test_install.py's assertion that the two agree.

requirements.requirement: FR-4 / AC-4: Version report consumable directly by another program, the supported compatibility judgement, needing no project, no model credential and no particular working directory.
requirements.note: Stated in README and docs/install.md; engine_version documents the same contract and client_cli.write emits exactly one JSON object; a failure exits non-zero with the reason on stderr and an empty version.

requirements.requirement: FR-5 / AC-5: How the version a configured source or release ref would provide is determined before anything is installed, and that this is what an installed engine is compared against.
requirements.note: `sh install.sh --resolve` described as answering without installing or changing anything; install.sh documents --resolve as producing the version on stdout, and the existing Inputs table explains FORGEL_SOURCE/FORGEL_REF.

requirements.requirement: FR-6 / AC-6: Strictly-newer comparison rule; equal or older available version leaves the installed engine untouched.
requirements.note: Both files state the rule and scope it correctly: `sh install.sh` installs the target it resolved, so the comparison belongs to the caller that keeps the engine current. This is consistent with the shipped installer rather than a false claim about it.

requirements.requirement: FR-7 / AC-7: How to remove the engine and its entry point and which configuration and project material are kept.
requirements.note: `sh install.sh --uninstall` removes the install root, the entry point and the start-up block; `~/.forgel` configuration and project material are kept, consistent with the README's documented engine home.

requirements.requirement: FR-8 / AC-8: Every name, option, location and example matches the shipped engine and installer; no documented behaviour they do not perform.
requirements.note: Checked against install.sh (inputs, defaults, modes, stdout contract, start-up markers), engine_version.py (--json/--home handling, failure behaviour) and client_cli.py (flat envelope). The only imprecision is the `$FORGEL_BIN_DIR` wording, which is contextualised by the correct default path in the same section.

requirements.requirement: FR-9 / AC-9: User-visible release notes carry an entry covering the install step, entry point and reachability, removal, the directly consumable version inquiry and pre-install version determination.
requirements.note: The new CHANGELOG.md 'Added' entries cover each of the five required capabilities; the header matches the format the release train generates.

requirements.requirement: FR-10 / AC-10: Behaviour and stable contracts only; no internal structure, timing, runtime bound, test duration or local environment detail.
requirements.note: The new text names only user-facing inputs and observable outcomes; no timings, bounds, internal module structure or test details appear.

requirements.requirement: FR-11 / AC-11: No statement in the user-facing introduction contradicts the shipped installer or version behaviour, and no previously accurate section is weakened.
requirements.note: README's Install section was corrected and its removed equivalence claim (installer output equals `forgel version --json`) is restated in the new 'Confirming the installation' section; the rest of the introduction (client, scripted client, skeleton, gates) is untouched.

requirements.requirement: Constraints: documentation-only change, no automated check on documentation, no release version or tag assignment, no unrelated files.
requirements.note: Only CHANGELOG.md, README.md and docs/install.md changed; no test or guard reads documentation, no test was removed or weakened, and no version or tag is assigned or promised.
